one_liner: AVX-512 IFMA BLS12-381 optimal ate pairing built on blst; about 1.9x lower single-pairing latency than blst's x64 assembly.
what_it_does: avxbls computes the optimal ate pairing on BLS12-381 (Miller loop plus final exponentiation), the core of BLS signature verification and pairing-based SNARK verifiers. It is a research code base forked in spirit from blst: it reuses blst's types (POINTonE1_affine, POINTonE2_affine, vec384fp12), its scalar field code and x64 assembly, and replaces the hot Miller-loop and final-exponentiation steps with vectorized versions. The exposed functions are miller_loop_n, final_exp and optimal_ate_pairing in src/pairing.h; the Makefile only builds test and bench executables, so there is no library target or blst-named API.
how_it_is_fast: Fp elements are held in radix 2^48 (8 limbs x 48 bits = 384 bits) inside 64-bit lanes so that AVX-512 IFMA's 52x52-bit multiply-accumulate (vpmadd52lo/hi) leaves 4 bits of headroom for lazy carry propagation; Montgomery multiplication and reduction run 8 lanes wide. The paper's contribution is choosing vectorization granularities per tower level (layouts named 8x1w, 4x2w, 2x2x2w, 1x4x2w in fp12_avx.h) so that independent Fp/Fp2 operations inside line doubling/addition, Fp12 squaring and cyclotomic squaring fill the 8 lanes, with values converted between blst's 64-bit radix and the 48-bit radix at step boundaries. Final exponentiation uses Granger-Scott cyclotomic squaring by default or Karabina-style compressed cyclotomic squaring via the COMPRESSED_CYCLOTOMIC_SQR compile-time switch.
when_to_use: Latency of a single BLS12-381 pairing matters (one signature verification, one pairing check) on a CPU with AVX-512 IFMA: Intel Ice Lake, Tiger Lake, Sapphire Rapids or later Xeons, or AMD Zen 4/Zen 5.
You already build on blst and can vendor its field code, swapping in the vectorized Miller loop and final exponentiation.
As a reference for how to map extension-field tower arithmetic onto 8-lane IFMA when writing your own pairing or BN254 code.
Research or benchmarking where reproducing the TCHES 2025 numbers against blst on the same machine is the goal (both sides ship with identical gcc flags).
when_not_to_use: Multi-pairing products (n > 1, e.g. aggregate BLS verification): the default vectorized Miller-loop step add_n_dbl_n_vector reads only T[0], Q[0] and Px2[0] and ignores n, so miller_loop_n with n > 1 does not compute the product of pairings.
CPUs without AVX-512 IFMA (Intel client cores from Alder Lake on, older Xeons, Arm): there is no fallback path, and the build uses -march=native so binaries are not portable.

Production signing/verification stacks: no library build, no hash-to-curve, signature API or subgroup/input validation in the pairing entry points, no side-channel claims, 9 stars and last commit 2025-09-27.
Throughput-bound batch verification: it is latency-optimized for one pairing; a batch-oriented design such as VROOM's RNS approach may fit better.

integration.dependencies: none beyond the bundled blst-derived sources (src/assembly.S, fields, points, recip) and src/rdtsc64.S for timing
integration.min_toolchain: gcc with AVX-512 IFMA intrinsics (Makefile: gcc -O3 -fomit-frame-pointer -m64 -mbmi2 -march=native -fwrapv -mtune=native); C99 for VLAs in miller_loop_n; gcc version not stated
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX-512F and AVX-512 IFMA plus BMI2/ADX (Linux/ELF toolchain assumed by the -z noexecstack flag)
integration.thread_safety: not documented (functions are pure on caller buffers; no global mutable state seen in pairing.c)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same data types and math as blst's internal pairing code, but different function names, no blst public API (blst_miller_loop, pairing context) and single-pair only in the vectorized Miller loop

gotchas: miller_loop_n/optimal_ate_pairing accept n but the vectorized Miller loop only processes the first (P, Q) pair; start_dbl_n loops over n, so results for n > 1 are silently wrong rather than rejected.
The faster 1,195,236-cycle variant needs COMPRESSED_CYCLOTOMIC_SQR set to 1 in src/pairing.h; the default build is the Granger-Scott path (1,265,314 cycles in the paper).

The bundled test checks bilinearity identities (e(P,[k]Q) == e([k]P,Q) and two variants) with a fixed scalar inside the same implementation; it does not compare output against blst or known-answer vectors.
Cycle counts come from rdtsc over 10000 iterations after 1000 warm-up calls; on CPUs where rdtsc ticks at a fixed reference rate, turbo and AVX-512 frequency licensing affect the reading.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Against VROOM (also AVX-512 IFMA BLS12-381 versus blst), pick avxbls when you want plain Montgomery arithmetic in radix 2^48 tuned for single-pairing latency and a peer-reviewed TCHES result; pick VROOM for its RNS formulation or broader curve coverage (BN254). The GMP-oriented siblings (ctbignum, intx, mp++) do not implement pairings.
verified_claims_summary: The TCHES 2025(4) paper by Cheng, Fotiadis, Grossschaedl and Page (read only through search-result abstracts; tches.iacr.org and eprint.iacr.org are blocked here) reports a full BLS12-381 optimal ate pairing in 1,265,314 cycles (Granger-Scott) or 1,195,236 cycles (compressed cyclotomic squaring) versus 2,351,615 cycles for blst's scalar x64 assembly, 1.86x and 1.97x, on an Intel Core i3-1005G1 (Ice Lake). Both sides are built with the same gcc -O3 -march=native flags in the repo (Makefile and baseline/Makefile) and timed with rdtsc; the gcc version and turbo settings were not readable here.
status_note: Apache-2.0 research artifact (230 commits, last 2025-09-27, 9 stars) with no releases or library target; small enough to vendor for single-pairing latency work, but fix or avoid the n > 1 path and validate against blst before relying on it.
